parts:
Hi, 

I have (a probably stupid) question ... 

If in my model i have :
 model{
  for(i in 1: n_obs) {
    mu <- a*x + b 
   y[i] ~ Normal(mu, sigma)
  }
}


If extract mu, and extract parameters estimate to compute new ypred.
Logically mu extracted values from stanfit object, and the mean of ypred would be similar ?

But for one of my model (Stock-recruitment) this is not the case... 

Many thanks in advance for your responses.
And sorry for this probably stupid question.
Colin

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Difference between mu and a posteriori estimates
parts:
Stan's samplers report the posterior mean for parameters,
whereas max a posteriori reports the posterior mode. These
are often not the same and the mean often exists when the mode
doesn't. The posterior mean minimizes expected square error of
the estimate---posterior mode doesn't have the same interpretability
as an expectation.

But if you want to do Bayesian posterior predictive inference,
you need to average over the posterior, which you can do in
generated quantities to compute the relevant integral. This
is the measure that gives you the correct uncertainty calibration
relative to your model. Look at the section titled "Prediction"
in the Stan manual chapter on regression; there's an explanation
of the integral being computed in the chapter on Bayesian Data
Analysis.

- Bob
